[[Category:Launcher (Primary)]] {{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|The custom weapon of a fearsome Kuva Lich. Unlike the basic version the Kuva Ogris fires detonite-infused casing semi-automatically, from a smaller magazine, while dealing greater damage per shot}} The '''Kuva Ogris''' is the [[Kuva (Variant)|Kuva]] variant of the {{Weapon|Ogris}} rocket launcher, firing rounds in a semi-automatic fashion rather than a short charge-up and with increased damage and [[status chance]], with its damage altered to include physical types, but has much worse [[ammo]] economy. ==Characteristics== *This weapon does primarily {{D|Blast}} damage. *Direct hits have a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc. *Rockets explode in a '''7.9''' meter radius upon impact with a surface or enemy. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. **Enemies can destroy the rockets with gunfire or area of effect explosions. *Can be fired while sprinting. *Can use the Ogris-exclusive {{M|Nightwatch Napalm}} mod, and the launcher-exclusive {{M|Adhesive Blast}} mod. *Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. *Adversary Weapon: **Comes with an additional bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, or {{D|Radiation}} damage, based on the Kuva Lich's [[Adversary System/Progenitor|progenitor Warframe]], which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%. ***[[Valence Fusion]] can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%). **[[Polarization|Polarizing]] the weapon increases its max [[rank]] by '''2''', capping at rank '''40''' after '''5''' polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity. **{{Resource|Elemental Vice}} can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely. **Listed [[Mastery Rank]] requirement is not enforced - the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Kuva Lich that has this weapon equipped. {{Advantages|class=Launcher| }} {{Disadvantages|class=Launcher| *Projectiles have travel time. *Extremely poor ammo economy. **Very low magazine size of just 3 rounds; requires frequent reloading. **Very small ammo capacity; requires just 3 reloads to fully deplete all ammo reserves. **Only restores 1 unit of ammunition per ammo pickup. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 20% from central impact. }} {{WeaponComparison|Ogris}} **Trigger type (Semi vs Charge) ==Acquisition== {{Transclude|Adversary System/Weapons#Kuva Acquisition}} ==Notes== {{Transclude|Adversary System#Notes}} {{Transclude|Adversary System/Progenitor}} ==Tips== *The weapon's poor ammo economy can be mitigated with {{M|Vigilante Supplies}}, {{M|Ammo Drum}}, and/or {{Companion|Carrier}}'s {{M|Ammo Case}}. **Pairing {{M|Vigilante Supplies}} with {{Arcane|Primary Compression}} for its (up to) 50% [[Ammo Efficiency]] completely fixes the ammo economy. Even missions with low enemy density will drop plenty of ammo to keep your Kuva Ogris well-supplied. *Installing {{M|Nightwatch Napalm}} grants the Kuva Ogris an effective crowd control capability, as the lingering flames deal {{D|Heat}} damage which procs Heat status, briefly stunning those who are affected. **As [[Railjack]] [[Railjack/Crew|Crewmates]] use player weapons ''with their mod configurations'', handing them a Kuva Ogris with Nightwatch Napalm makes them a crucial crowd control support when needed, as they can sustain the lingering flames indefinitely, since they do not need ammo. **{{A|Toxic Lash}} will apply {{D|Toxin}} damage, and a guaranteed Toxin status, every time [[Nightwatch Napalm]] damages an enemy. This ''dramatically'' increases the weapon's overall damage output. ==Media== Kuva Ogris 2.png|Kuva Ogris as shown in the arsenal Kuva Ogris 1.png {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|39}} *Fixed performance issues caused by Kuva Ogris’ explosion lights. {{ver|38.6}} *Fixed performance issues caused by Kuva Ogris’ SFX while Adhesive Blast is equipped. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 1 Ammo per Pick Up: *Kuva Ogris '''Many weapons have also had their maximum ammo capacity adjusted.''' Primary Weapons: *Kuva Ogris: From 30 to 7 ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|29.6.6}} *Fixed equipping Unreal Skins to Kuva weapons overriding their stats to perform like their base version. {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Kuva Ogris: 80% {{ver|27.2.1}} *Decreased the distance to point of impact that Self Stagger is inflicted with the Shedu due to having a large AoE range. {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' {{ver|26.0.7}} *Damage increased from 454 to 714. *Explosion damage changed from 427 Blast to 159 Puncture, 275 Slash, and 253 Blast (undocumented). *Fixed Kuva Lich weapons that do damage on both impact and explosion (Kuva Ogris, Kuva Ayanga, etc) doing significantly less overall damage than expected. This was due to the Elemental bonus only being applied to the "on impact" of the projectile itself and not the explosion. {{ver|26}} *Introduced. }} {{ver/Lu|26}} ==See also== *{{Weapon|Ogris}}, the normal counterpart of this weapon. *{{Weapon|Tenet Envoy}}, the Tenet equivalent rocket launcher. {{WeaponNav}} [[es:Ogris Kuva]] [[Category:Launcher]] [[Category:Grineer]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Update 26]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Grineer Weapons]] [[Category:Augmented Weapons]] [[uk:Оґріс-кува]] [[Category:Blast Damage Weapons]]

the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Kuva Lich that has this weapon equipped. {{Advantages|class=Launcher| *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. **{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon, especially in combination with [[Multishot]] mods. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Launcher| *Grenades have travel time and heavy arcing. *Extremely low magazine capacity of just 1 round, requires frequent reloading. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 30% from central impact. }} {{WeaponComparison|Tonkor}} ==Acquisition== {{Transclude|Adversary System/Weapons#Kuva Acquisition}} ==Notes== *When Multishot mods and {{M|Heavy Caliber}} are equipped on this weapon, one of the grenades will fly towards the point of aim while the rest of the grenades will fan out horizontally and explode close to the point of aim. This helps in giving a single shot of grenades a larger effective AoE, especially if {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) is also loaded, as well as bigger damage on enemies near the point of impact. *While its standard counterpart's grenades fizzle out when shot at too close ranges and hitting someone due to the arming distance mechanic, the Kuva Tonkor's shots explode on impact even at point blank range, making it more reliable at dealing massive damage at close ranges. It does give a risk at staggering the user. {{Transclude|Adversary System#Notes}} {{Transclude|Adversary System/Progenitor}} ==Tips== *With {{M|Primed Magazine Warp}}, the Kuva Tonkor will have {{Math|1 {{mul}} (1 + 55%)|t=y|bf-a=y}}, rounded to '''2''' magazine capacity, giving it a higher overall DPS rate. *As with the standard Tonkor, the Kuva Tonkor's high critical chance makes it a good candidate for {{M|Hunter Munitions}}. *While the Kuva Tonkor's shots lack the cluster-bomb effects of the {{Weapon|Kuva Bramma}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Zarr}}, its very large ammo reserves (for a launcher-type primary) and comparable damage grant it a better ability for sustained crowd control in endless [[The Steel Path|Steel Path]] missions, especially when loaded with ammo conversion mods such as {{M|Vigilante Supplies}}. ==Trivia== *The [[Grineer Language|Grineer text]] on the side of its barrel {{GrineerScript|RAVAGE}} translates to "Ravage". ==Media== Kuva Tonkor 1.png|Kuva Tonkor as shown in the arsenal Kuva Tonkor 2.png Kuva Tonkor 3.png {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32.3}} *Fixed a Tonkor grenade appearing in the player's hand for the duration of the mission if they happen to roll and reload at just the right time. **''This fixes the issue while using both the Tonkor and Kuva Tonkor.'' {{ver|32.2}} *Reduced the flare size of the Kuva Tonkor’s explosion. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. {{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|A highly-optimized Nukor that allows for the weapon’s microwave field to hit up to two additional targets.}} The '''Kuva Nukor''' is the [[Kuva (Variant)|Kuva]] variant of the {{Weapon|Nukor}}, with improvements to its already high [[critical multiplier]] and [[status chance]], and increased [[critical chance]], magazine, and range, but with marginally lower damage. Its beam has also gained the ability to chain between multiple enemies. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Radiation}} damage. *Highest [[critical multiplier]] of all weapons in the game. *Can inflict a unique status effect called {{D|Microwave}}, enlarging the body part that was shot at. * [[Continuous Weapon]]: **Shoots a beam with a range of '''29''' meters. **Consumes 0.5 ammo per tick of damage. **Takes 0.6 seconds of firing to ramp up the damage from 30% to 100%. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 30% over 2 seconds. *Beam can chain up to '''2''' nearby enemies within '''9''' meters from the initial target, each doing '''50%''' of the main beam's damage. **Enemy corpses will still allow the beam to connect to nearby enemies. *Adversary Weapon: **Comes with an additional bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, or {{D|Radiation}} damage, based on the Kuva Lich's [[Adversary System/Progenitor|progenitor Warframe]], which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%. ***[[Valence Fusion]] can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%). **[[Polarization|Polarizing]] the weapon increases its max [[rank]] by '''2''', capping at rank '''40''' after '''5''' polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity. **{{Resource|Elemental Vice}} can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely. **Listed [[Mastery Rank]] requirement is not enforced - the weapon may theoretically be obtained at any mastery rank by acquiring and vanquishing a Kuva Lich that has this weapon equipped. {{Advantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held| *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held| }} {{WeaponComparison|Nukor}} ==Acquisition== {{Transclude|Adversary System/Weapons#Kuva Acquisition}} ==Notes== *The Kuva Nukor can proc an invisible [[Status Effect]] called Microwave that causes the part of the enemy hit to become larger. **Microwave procs have infinite duration, but the visual effect does not. **Microwave counts as an individual status for {{M|Condition Overload}}, {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}}, {{M|Galvanized Savvy}}, and {{M|Galvanized Shot}}. **Some enemies are not affected by this [[Status Effect]], at least visually, for example [[Liches]] *Upon striking an enemy, the beam chains up to '''2''' enemies within '''9''' meters of the main target. Each chain beam does '''50%''' of the main beam's damage. **Headshotting the original target does not affect the chain damage. **The beam '''will not''' chain to a [[Nullifier Crewman|Nullifier]] through its shield should it connect with a target outside or partially enclosed by it. **The beam can also continue to chain to enemies even if targeting a dead enemy or an enemy who is dead but in a dying animation. **Compared to its Tenet counterpart, the {{Weapon|Tenet Cycron}}, that chains within '''7''' meters at '''60%''' of its main damage, the Kuva Nukor generally deals less damage albeit at a longer range. But this is not considering the critical stat differences between the two weapons, as while the former got a far higher critical chance stat (20% against 7%), the latter has a far superior critical multiplier stat (1.8x against 5x). *[[Punch Through]] will cause the main beam to chain independently from each additional target hit, potentially doubling or tripling the total damage output when fired into a crowd. The chain from the target hit after the Punch Through can deal damage to the first target, and vice versa. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6q7joP80Y1U Youtube : Warframe | Kuva Nukor and Punch Through] *The beam can damage [[Rampart]] from the front. {{Transclude|Adversary System#Notes}} {{Transclude|Adversary System/Progenitor}} ==Tips== *While its base critical chance is low, {{M|Primed Pistol Gambit}}/{{M|Creeping Bullseye}} will allow the weapon to critically hit '''~20.1%'''/'''21%''' of the time, enough to benefit from the very high critical multiplier. *Absolute critical chance bonuses such as {{Arcane|Secondary Enervate}}, {{Arcane|Arcane Avenger}} or {{A|Covenant}} are particularly effective with this weapon, to benefit from the crit multiplier without be limited by the low base critical chance. *You can shoot corpses to use them as "conduits" that can chain the beam to other enemies. ==Media== {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|UbpFE85gwko|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|38}} *Fixed script error caused by the Microwave Status Effect VFX. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''

{{Codex|During parades and victory marches, the Laetum fired pigmented airburst rounds that rained onto festive crowds. The Orokin sent Laetum with the Zariman so they could properly celebrate a successful maiden voyage to Tau. There would be no such celebration, but the Void imbued the Laetum with a much more explosive capacity.}}
'''Laetum''' is an [[Incarnon]] ceremonial pistol evolved by the [[Void]] to shoot deadly explosive airburst rounds. Starting out as a semi-automatic pistol, achieving enough weakpoint hits will allow the player to temporarily transform it into a fully automatic rifle that deals {{D|Radiation}} damage in a small area of effect.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Slash}} damage in its normal form and {{D|Radiation}} in its Incarnon Form.
*As an [[Incarnon]] weapon, Laetum has '''5''' evolution tiers with different perks that allow players to customize their Laetum's stats.
**Once Incarnon Form is unlocked, landing [[Enemy Body Parts|weakpoint hits]] fill the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that transforms the Laetum into an automatic weapon via the [[Alternate Fire]] key.
***Additional shots from [[Multishot]] counts as separate weakpoint hits.
***The gauge reaches full charge after '''12''' weakpoint hits, and does not require a full gauge to activate. It will also emit a small, ghost-like wail when the gauge is completely full.
***Shots deal pure {{D|Impact}} damage on direct hits, and {{D|Radiation}} damage in a '''2''' meter radius.
****Initial hit and explosion apply status separately.
****Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls.
****Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}).
***Instead of drawing from the Laetum's ammo reserves, Incarnon Form gives the Laetum a unique "magazine" from '''18''' rounds per charge to a maximum of '''216''', indicated by the regular ammo HUD and a bar underneath the reticle.
****If the [[Alternate Fire]] key is pressed whether or not the Incarnon magazine is fully expended, the Laetum is transformed back into its default state, however this will also fully expend any remaining Incarnon gauge.

{{Advantages}}
{{Disadvantages|
*Incarnon Form:
**Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]].
**Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions.
**Explosion have linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 80% from central impact.
**Cannot Punch-Through.}}

==Acquisition==
Laetum's main blueprint is purchased from [[Cavalero]] of [[The Holdfasts]] at '''Rank 0 - Neutral''' for {{sc|3,000}} Standing. The blueprint can be [[Trading|traded]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Incarnon Form==
When newly acquired from the [[Foundry]], players must acquire '''100''' kills with the Laetum in order to gain access to its Incarnon transformation. Each challenge additionally grants 5,000 [[affinity]] to the weapon, affected by [[Affinity Booster]]s. The following Evolution tiers, their requirements for unlocking them, and their related perks, are shown below.

====Overview====
*Incarnon Form is activated by filling the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that appears under the reticle by achieving [[Enemy Body Parts|weakpoint hits]] and then pressing the [[Alternate Fire]] button. '''12''' weakpoints will completely fill the gauge. A full gauge is not required to activate Incarnon Form.
**Charges do '''not''' generate on the backpacks of most [[MOA]] variants, or vulnerability spots generated by {{A|Sonar}} or {{M|Detect Vulnerability}} in places other than actual weakpoints.
**Weakpoints on corpses or [[Invulnerable]] targets do '''not''' build charges.
**Individual [[Multishot]] bullets can build charges.
*Mode switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation equal to the weapon's [[reload speed]].
**Swapping to and from Incarnon Form will fully reload the normal form's magazine.
*Instead of drawing ammunition from its reserves, the Laetum's Incarnon Form uses a separate "magazine" with each charge producing '''18''' rounds to a maximum of '''216'''. Once all ammunition is expended, the Laetum reverts to its normal form.
**Incarnon Form's magazine is '''not''' affected by mods.
**Incarnon Form is '''not''' affected by [[Ammo Efficiency]] (such as the '''Ruptured Plenitude''' or '''Agile Executor''' perks or {{A|Energized Munitions}}).
**Charges and Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as [[holster]]ing, [[bleedout]], or being [[disarm]]ed. However, charges and Incarnon Form are removed upon [[death]].

==Tips==
*Evolution II can be easily done solo in [[Elite Sanctuary Onslaught]], with the increased spawn rate of the Eximus enemies.
*Evolution III challenge can be made easier by increasing [[Magazine Capacity]] (with {{M|Slip Magazine}} ({{M|Primed Slip Magazine|Primed}}), {{M|Ice Storm}}, {{M|Tainted Clip}}, and/or {{M|Combo Fury}}) and by increasing [[Multishot]] (with {{M|Barrel Diffusion}} ({{M|Galvanized Diffusion|Galvanized}}) and/or {{M|Lethal Torrent}}).
*For Evolution III, with no other enemy around, turning [[Invisible]] reduces the Angel's activity, sometimes standing still. This makes it easier to land headshots.
*The Evolution III challenge cannot be completed using Laetum's Incarnon mode.
*The Evolution III challenge counts reloading on any weapon, not just the Laetum. This includes the [[Sirocco]] amp if equipped on the Operator.
*Using an [[Exalted Weapon]] will negate Evolution V challenge.
*Incarnon Genesis weapons are counted for Evolution V challenge.

==Trivia==
*''[[wiktionary:Laetum|Laetum]]'' is an inflection of the word ''[[wiktionary:laetus|laetus]]'', which means ''happy'' in Latin and reflects the Laetum's original purpose.
